findings.finding: The supplied receptor crop contains 308 heavy atoms within a reported 12 A radius around centroid [23.353, -30.938, 13.330] A; no atom coordinates or residue identities are provided.
Reported nearest protein-neighbor distance quantiles are 1.226, 1.371 and 3.896 A. These describe receptor geometry, not ligand contacts or ligand clashes; short values can include bonded neighbors.
There are no affinity labels or generated Steer observations. The available receptor summary supports geometric hypotheses but no association between steering parameters and target pIC50.

directions: Geometric hypothesis: compare contact_weight 0, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 with other settings fixed to test whether contact attraction improves occupancy without excessive crowding; no optimum is established.
Geometric hypothesis: compare repulsion_weight 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 at a fixed contact weight, measuring generated ligand-protein clashes and strain to assess the contact/repulsion tradeoff.

Control-strength hypothesis: compare native_rms_ratio 0.1, 0.2 and 0.33, then time_ramp_power 0, 1 and 2, changing one key at a time under the supplied protocol and assessing final predicted pIC50, strain and graph transitions.
limitations: Aggregate crop statistics cannot resolve pocket accessibility, contact sites, chemical complementarity or per-atom force directions.
The pocket field is an untyped geometric proxy; improved contacts or fewer clashes do not establish improved affinity.
No ligand reward template, generated candidates, historical comparisons or affinity labels are supplied; enrichment, survival and temporal trends cannot be estimated.
Directions are untested hypotheses. Single-seed comparisons are exploratory; there is no evidence-based winner. Only the four pocket-supported update keys apply.
